# manual capture -- NOT a probe, not scored by match.json
# issue: 8725
# what: the source asymmetry that explains why plain TraceRay is unaffected while
#       dx::HitObject::Invoke asserts, with the IR contrast that demonstrates it.
# exe: <repo>/build/Debug/bin/dxc.exe
# version: dxcompiler.dll: 1.10(5433-ab540090)(1.9.0.5433) - 1.9.0.5433 (triage, ab5400907)
# tree: DirectXShaderCompiler at ab5400907
# ran: 2026-08-07 (this session)

The report says "it also appears specific to HitObject::Invoke: the same shader
using TraceRay instead compiles fine". That is correct, and the reason is a
difference between the two functions that build intrinsic declarations in Sema.
Both intrinsics declare the payload as `inout udt Payload`
(utils/hct/gen_intrin_main.txt:311 for TraceRay, :1141 for Invoke, :1140 for
dx::HitObject::TraceRay), so the difference is not in the intrinsic table.

### A. Free-function intrinsics -- tools/clang/lib/Sema/SemaHLSL.cpp:2123-2135
###    (AddHLSLIntrinsicFunction, declared at :2102)

  for (size_t i = 1; i < functionArgTypeCount; i++) {
    // Change out/inout param to reference type.
    if (paramMods[i - 1].isAnyOut() ||
        paramMods[i - 1].GetKind() == hlsl::ParameterModifier::Kind::Ref) {
      QualType Ty = functionArgQualTypes[i];
      // Aggregate type will be indirect param convert to pointer type.
      // Don't need add reference for it.
      if ((!Ty->isArrayType() && !Ty->isRecordType()) ||
          hlsl::IsHLSLVecMatType(Ty)) {
        functionArgQualTypes[i] = context.getLValueReferenceType(Ty);
      }
    }
  }

`Payload` is a record type and not a vector/matrix, so the inner guard is false
and TraceRay's payload parameter stays `Payload` -- NOT `Payload &`.

### B. Object/class method intrinsics -- SemaHLSL.cpp:6334-6340
###    (AddHLSLIntrinsicMethod, declared at :6296, called from :11434)

  for (unsigned int i = 1; i < parameterTypeCount; i++) {
    // Change out/inout parameter type to rvalue reference type.
    if (paramMods[i - 1].isAnyOut()) {
      parameterTypes[i] =
          m_context->getLValueReferenceType(parameterTypes[i]);
    }
  }

No record-type guard. dx::HitObject::Invoke is a static class method
([[static,class_prefix]]), so it is built here and its payload parameter becomes
`Payload &`.

### C. Why that turns into the assert

CGCall.cpp:2961-2962 asserts `type->isReferenceType() == E->isGLValue()`.
EmitHLSLOutParamConversionInit has already replaced the argument with a
DeclRefExpr built VK_RValue, because the payload is an aggregate
(CGHLSLMS.cpp:6384-6392). So:

  TraceRay   type = `Payload`    (not a reference) == !isGLValue()  -> holds
  Invoke     type = `Payload &`  (a reference)     != !isGLValue()  -> ASSERTS

and with asserts off the mismatch continues into the by-value aggregate path,
CreateLoad (CGCall.cpp:3411) + CreateBitCast (CGCall.cpp:3429), which is the
invalid `bitcast <struct value> to <struct pointer>`.

### D. The IR contrast, measured

$ dxc -T lib_6_9 -fcgl variant-traceray-byval.hlsl        # plain TraceRay, exit 0

  define internal void @"\01?Function@@YAXUPayload@@@Z"(%struct.Payload* %p) #0 {
    %0 = alloca %struct.Payload
    ...
    call void @llvm.memcpy.p0i8.p0i8.i64(i8* %7, i8* %8, i64 4, i32 1, i1 false)   ; copy in to %0
    call void @"dx.hl.op..void (i32, %dx.types.Handle, i32, i32, i32, i32, i32, %struct.RayDesc*, %struct.Payload*)"(
        i32 69, %dx.types.Handle %11, i32 0, i32 1, i32 2, i32 4, i32 0,
        %struct.RayDesc* %ray, %struct.Payload* %0)                                ; ADDRESS of %0 passed
    call void @llvm.memcpy.p0i8.p0i8.i64(i8* %12, i8* %13, i64 4, i32 1, i1 false) ; copy out of %0

  One temporary, and its POINTER is handed to the HL op. The copy-in/copy-out
  conversion happened here too -- so that path is not by itself the defect.

$ dxc -T lib_6_9 -fcgl repro.hlsl                          # HitObject::Invoke
  (manual-case-fcgl-invalid-bitcast.txt CASE 7; asserts continued past)

    ... memcpy   %1 <- %p            ; the out-param conversion temp
    ... memcpy   %2 <- %1            ; a SECOND, agg temp, from EmitAnyExprToTemp
    %12 = load %struct.Payload, %struct.Payload* %2
    %13 = bitcast %struct.Payload %12 to %struct.Payload*    ; <-- invalid
    call void @"dx.hl.op..void (i32, %dx.types.HitObject*, %struct.Payload*)"(
        i32 382, %dx.types.HitObject* %obj, %struct.Payload* %13)

  The second temporary is the tell: EmitCallArg took the reference-type branch,
  materialised the r-value into a fresh aggregate temp, and EmitCall then had to
  coerce that aggregate to the pointer the HL function type wants.

### E. Both conditions are necessary

The reference-typed parameter alone is harmless, and so is the copy-in temporary
alone. It takes both:

  control-inout.hlsl        inout param -> %struct.Payload* noalias %p -> SafeToSkip
                            (CGHLSLMS.cpp:6355), no temp, no VK_RValue expr   -> clean
  variant-local-direct.hlsl local payload, alloca -> SafeToSkip
                            (CGHLSLMS.cpp:6347), no temp                      -> clean
  variant-traceray-byval    temp created, but the parameter is not a reference -> clean
  repro.hlsl                by-value param: temp created AND parameter is a reference -> ASSERT
  variant-static-global     mutable global: temp created AND reference        -> ASSERT
  variant-ho-traceray-byval also a class method, so also a reference          -> ASSERT

Measured, not inferred -- `dxc -T lib_6_9 -fcgl variant-local-direct.hlsl` emits no
memcpy and no temporary at all, just the alloca:

  %p = alloca %struct.Payload, align 4
  call void @"dx.hl.op..void (i32, %dx.types.HitObject*, %struct.Payload*)"(
      i32 382, %dx.types.HitObject* %obj, %struct.Payload* %p)

### F. Scope this implies (stated as a lead, not a measured claim)

Any *object/class method* intrinsic with an `out`/`inout` parameter of record type
is built by path B and so has a reference-typed parameter. Only dx::HitObject's
Invoke and TraceRay were measured here; whether other object methods can be
reached with a non-SafeToSkip aggregate argument was not enumerated.
